text_snippet: Social Work & Society Open Menu Social Work & Society Social Work & Society Current Issue Vol. 24 No. 1 (2026): Urbanisation, Sanitation, and Social Justice in South Asia: Addressing Inequities Through Social Work and Policy Interventions Social work is historically as well as currently related to urbanisation. This is true for different contexts around the globe since the 19 th century. The fundamental political-economic and socio-cultural transformations, called industrialisation and modernisation, had been and are still characterised as a spatial concentration: People move from more rural areas to the cities and existing cities grow – sometimes massively, like the so called mega cities, not at least in Asia and North as well as South America, can show in the last decades. Issues of housing, of vocational training, childcare or care of elderly have to be answered in the urban context in a different way. But living conditions and public infrastructure is not only a question of these conditions of living and education. At the same time all this is based on ensuring sanitation. Otherwise, not only combating sources of infection and similar hazards moves to the forefront. But people would be also faced with the need to ensure sanitation themselves, what is more or less impossible.
